fragments.quote_excerpt: This section describes each PTX instruction. In addition to the name and the format of the instruction, the semantics are described, followed by some examples that attempt to show several possible instantiations of the instruction.

In PTX, predicate registers are virtual and have .pred as the type specifier. So, predicate registers can be declared as .reg .pred p, q, r; All instructions have an optional guard predicate which controls conditional execution of the instruction. The syntax to specify conditional execution is to prefix an instruction with @{!}p , where p is a predicate variable, optionally negated. Instructions without a guard predicate are executed unconditionally.

types.compatibility_rules: Operand types and sizes are checked against instruction types for compatibility. Two fundamental types are compatible if they have the same basic type and are the same size; signed and unsigned integer types are compatible if they have the same size; the bit-size type is compatible with any fundamental type of the same size. state_reads.component: guard predicate register p (when a guard is present)
state_reads.description: The value of the predicate register referenced by the guard is read to evaluate the complete guard expression. The section 9.3 predicated-execution context states that an optional guard predicate controls conditional execution and that the syntax prefixes an instruction with @{!}p, where p is a predicate variable, optionally negated (CTX-02); the general predication form of section 9.7.13.2 executes for threads whose guard predicate is True (CTX-08); the guard read is the predicate value used by that evaluation.

state_writes.component: destination register d (on execution with a real destination register)
state_writes.description: When the complete guard expression evaluates true and d is a register, the destination register d is updated with the bitwise-and of the values read from source operands a and b. Only the destination update required by the bounded semantics is proposed: no other value register, predicate register, carry flag, or status/condition-code component is written by the bounded base and.b32.

When the destination is the bit bucket '_', the represented consequence is that no value register is written (the result is discarded). This is supported only to the strength of the general section 9.2 rule, which is recorded in the architecture (SF-A13) but is NOT present in this bundle; scalar and.b32-specific demonstration is absent (open question PTX-AND-SEM2-062).

Threads with a False guard predicate do nothing.' guard_semantics.guard_expression_representation: An optional guard prefix @{!}p appears to the left of the instruction, where p is a predicate register variable of type .pred, optionally negated with '!'. This is evidenced by the section 9.3 predicated-execution context (CTX-02): 'All instructions have an optional guard predicate which controls conditional execution of the instruction. The syntax to specify conditional execution is to prefix an instruction with @{!}p, where p is a predicate variable, optionally negated. Instructions without a guard predicate are executed unconditionally.' Predicate registers are virtual, have .pred as the type specifier, and can be declared as '.reg .pred p, q, r;' (CTX-02); predicate variables may only be declared in the register state space (CTX-05). The section 9.7 intro states the general predicability rule: 'All PTX instructions may be predicated. In the following descriptions, the optional guard predicate is omitted from the syntax.' (CTX-07). The general predication form is defined in section 9.7.13.2 (Control Flow Instructions: @): '@{!}p instruction;' with Description 'Execute an instruction or instruction block for threads that have the guard predicate True. Threads with a False guard predicate do nothing.' (CTX-08) and Semantics 'If {!}p then instruction' (CTX-08).

guard_expression_evaluation.no_guard: The complete guard expression is true; the instruction is executed unconditionally ('Instructions without a guard predicate are executed unconditionally.', CTX-02).
guard_expression_evaluation.at_p: @p: the complete guard expression is the value of predicate register p; execution occurs when p is true.
guard_expression_evaluation.at_bang_p: @!p: the complete guard expression is the logical negation of the value of predicate register p; execution occurs when p is false. The negated-guard semantics follows from the @{!}p syntax with p optionally negated (CTX-02); the general predication example '@!p div.f32 ratio,x,y // avoid division by zero' (CTX-08) shows the negated guard executing when the underlying predicate is false.
